title: RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation)
description: Learn how to build a complete retrieval pipeline—from chunking and embeddings to re-ranking—to provide Claude with precise, external context.
learning_objectives: Implement effective text chunking strategies for large documents
Generate and store vector embeddings in a vector database
Perform similarity searches to retrieve relevant context
Apply re-ranking techniques to improve retrieval precision
Construct an augmented prompt that integrates retrieved data for Claude

sections.heading: The RAG Architecture: Why and How
sections.content_brief: Explain the fundamental problem RAG solves (context window limits and hallucinations). Detail the high-level flow: Ingestion -> Retrieval -> Generation.

sections.heading: Data Preparation: Chunking Strategies
sections.content_brief: Discuss the importance of chunk size and overlap to maintain semantic meaning. Compare fixed-size chunking versus recursive character splitting.
sections.code_context: Implementing a recursive character text splitter to prepare documents for embedding.

sections.heading: Vector Embeddings and Storage
sections.content_brief: Explain how embeddings convert text into numerical vectors. Describe the role of vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, Milvus, or Chroma) in storing and indexing these vectors.
sections.code_context: Using an embedding model to vectorize text chunks and upserting them into a vector store.

sections.heading: Retrieval: Similarity Search
sections.content_brief: Explain the process of vectorizing a user query and performing a cosine similarity search. Discuss the 'Top-K' retrieval concept.
sections.code_context: Querying a vector database to retrieve the top 5 most relevant document chunks based on a user prompt.

sections.heading: Improving Precision with Re-ranking
sections.content_brief: Explain why initial retrieval can be noisy and how re-rankers (Cross-Encoders) refine the results. Describe the process of scoring retrieved documents against the query more rigorously.
sections.code_context: Implementing a re-ranking step to sort the top-K results by actual relevance score before passing them to the LLM.

sections.heading: End-to-End Example: Building a Knowledge Base Assistant
sections.content_brief: A concrete step-by-step walkthrough showing the full sequence from user input through each intermediate step (chunking, embedding, retrieval, re-ranking) to final output using Claude.
sections.code_context: A complete script integrating all pipeline stages into a single function that takes a question and returns an answer based on private data.

admonitions.content: Too small chunks lose context; too large chunks introduce noise. Always test your chunk size against the specific nature of your documents.
Re-ranking is computationally more expensive than similarity search. Only re-rank a small subset (e.g., top 20) of the initial retrieval results.
